sections.title: A past tense for a present wish
sections.content: You know how to soften a request with the *condicional* from A2 Unit 26: *¿Podría cambiar mi habitación?*, *Me gustaría pedir agua.* Spanish has one more polite form: the *imperfecto*. When you say *Quería pedirle un favor*, you do not mean that you wanted it in the past. You want it now, but the past tense keeps the wish at a polite distance, as if it were not pressing the other person. It is common in shops, offices and on the phone, with the verbs of wanting, coming, calling and wondering.

sections.title: Polite imperfect
rows: "I wanted to ask you a favour": you ask now.
Venía a preguntar por el horario.
"I have come to ask about the timetable": you are standing there now.
"I'm calling to confirm the appointment": the call is happening now.
Me preguntaba si usted podía ayudarme.
"I was wondering if you could help me": a request, not a story.

items.spanish: Buenas tardes, quería pedirle una cita con el doctor.
items.english: Good afternoon, I would like to ask you for an appointment with the doctor.

items.spanish: Disculpe, venía a preguntar por el horario de los trenes.
items.english: Excuse me, I have come to ask about the train timetable.

items.spanish: Hola, Marta, llamaba para preguntarte si puedes venir mañana.
items.english: Hi, Marta, I'm calling to ask if you can come tomorrow.

items.spanish: Me preguntaba si usted podría ayudarme con esto.
items.english: I was wondering if you could help me with this.

sections.content: The meaning is present, so only the situation tells you it is not a real past: a person standing at the counter who says *Venía a preguntar…* is asking now. The polite imperfect is used across the Spanish-speaking world, and only for your own wish or request: it does not soften what other people want.
